## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 This cross-textual transmission is corroborated by DharmaNexus, which computes substantial Pali-internal text reuse between Thig 8.1 and SN 5 (§2.1–6.2 matching §7.2.1–7.5.2), as well as shared verses with the preceding *Cālātherīgāthā* (Thig 7.2, §7.1–9.1 matching §5.4–8.1) and the commentary *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus aligns the text with the Chinese translation of the *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100, fascicle 12) [DharmaNexus], which is also listed in comparative tables of early Buddhist parallels to the *Sīsūpacālātherīgāthā* [Bingenheimer, Studies in Agama Literature].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: SN 5.7 Upacālāsutta
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0509a) (§3.1–8.4 ↔ §2735–2751); Bhikkhunī Saṁyutta (SN 5) (§2.1–6.2 ↔ §7.2.1–7.5.2); Cālātherīgāthā (Thig 7.2) (§7.1–9.1 ↔ §5.4–8.1)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): 別譯雜阿含經 (ZH_T02_0100) [zh]
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database — Supplies automated text-reuse matches with SN 5, Thig 7.2, the Therīgāthā commentary, and the Bieyi za ahan jing (T 100).
- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Samyutta Nikaya (2003) — Discusses the differing authorship attributions and fragmentary verse correspondences between the Therīgāthā and the Bhikkhunī Saṁyutta.
- [Nyanaponika et al. 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha: Their Lives, Their Works, Their Legacy (2003) — Relates the biographical tradition of Sāriputta's three sisters and their encounters with Māra preserved in the Therīgāthā.
- [Bingenheimer, Studies in Agama Literature] Marcus Bingenheimer, Studies in Agama Literature: With Special Reference to the Shorter Chinese Saṁyuktāgama — Discusses divergences between the Therīgāthā and the Saṁyutta Nikāya for the three sisters and provides Chinese parallel correspondences.
